newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges end weaker with no bulls buying.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges end weaker with no bulls buying.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges ended on the weak side on Wednesday with no bulls seen buying and Russian cargoes were talked at steady to slightly weaker numbers, traders said.

High sulphur fuel barges were said to have traded at as low as $84 fob ARA in the afternoon after earlier deals at $84.50, $84.75 and $85 a tonne, but all the numbers were within the late trading range a day earlier.
Later, bids sank to $83 a tonne, some traders said, while others maintained that the market was at $84/$85.
A major that tried to push the market higher on Tuesday was not very active while a trading house that tried to push it in the opposite direction was absent.
"Artificially they tried to keep the market up for a couple of days. But bulls are not buying at this moment and there's no good demand," a second trader said.
He put demand in the Rotterdam area at 10,000 tonnes while others said it was 5,000 tonnes higher.

A second trader said: "It's a standoff, there's lack of bunker demand in Rotterdam and good demand in Antwerp. There seems good demand for tomorrow and then we will see if the bears or bulls are right."
Low sulphur barges were quietly talked at steady levels of around $95/$96 a tonne.
No deals were reported in high sulphur cargoes but traders said there were indications for Russian M-100 at two means plus $2 with buyers said to be up to $1.50 lower.
A high sulphur cargo was heard sold on Tuesday by an independent trader to a trading house at $81 cif Rotterdam, or $1 tonne lower than a deal on Monday.
A second deal was reported done on Tuesday at $80 cif but the buyer mentioned would not confirm or deny it.
One percent cargoes were talked a little weaker after swaps fell slightly and with buying interest thin.
One trader said buyers were in the low nineties and sellers in the mid-nineties. A major was heard offering its cargo at $94.50 and buying interest was coming in at $2 lower.
